title.narrative: Private Infrastructure Development Group core funding contributions financial year 2021-22 - 2024-25

description.narrative: The Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) works to mobilise private sector investment to assist developing countries in developing infrastructure vital to boosting their economic growth and combating poverty. Contributions from Australia through the PIDG Trust support PIDG organisations InfraCo Asia, GuarantCo and the PIDG Technical Assistance facility. InfraCo Asia is a donor funded infrastructure project developer that originates, develops and operates infrastructure assets, focusing on lower income countries. GuarantCo is a company funded by donors that provides local currency guarantees to local / regional banks and bond investors to enable infrastructure projects to raise medium and long-term debt finance. Technical Assistance focuses on ensuring gender mainstreaming, promoting high health and safety standards for infrastructure and benefiting the local environment near projects. The PIDG is a DFAT blended finance mechanism.

description.narrative: Ba Lai water treatment plant became operational in Q2, 2023. The water distribution system provides 24/7 piped and treated water to 16 communes and one industrial area in Ben Tre province Viet Nam, where individuals are highly dependent on the collection of rainwater for everyday use. 97% of customers are now able to access a secure household water connection for the first time, with 75% of customers living below the poverty line. The water treatment plant is providing up to 5,000 m3/day of drinking water to 24,000 customers. ‍ Surveys conducted with Ba Lai customers reported that 93% of customers have an improved quality of life and 72% of customers report improved health. ‍ “Life is more convenient as the direct water supply is available inside the house, eliminating the need to manually pump or carry water from a river. This saves physical effort and makes life easier.” – Female, 46

description.narrative: Construction on AquaOne’s Xuan Mai Water Plant in Hoa Binh, Vietnam commenced in late 2024. The first phase of the water treatment plant will have an initial water treatment capacity of 150,000 m3/day by 2025 and serve 53,000 households through a pipeline network across Hanoi, Luong Son and Hoa Binh. ‍ The project addresses both current and future climate vulnerabilities by providing a significant supply of clean water sourced from surface water reserves. By sourcing water from surface water reserves instead of groundwater, the project reduces the pressure on overexploited aquifers, helping to prevent land subsidence and mitigate saline intrusion. The water treatment plant project design includes protection against a one in 100-year flood event and follows local standards for wind loading to mitigate cyclone risks. ‍ More than 30% of the AquaOne workforce are female and 24% are in senior leadership positions. ‍ This project was supported by the Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG), which Australia co-owns alongside five other governments. PIDG is one of DFAT’s blended finance investments. ‍ The project was financed through a verified green, local currency bond which received investment from major institutional investors Chubb Life Vietnam, Hanwha Life, AIA, and Generali.

Guarantee facilities provided through the PIDG saw the 2023 launch of the inaugural gender bond in South Asia raised in local currency (Pakistani Rupee). The three-year gender bond will be used to finance women-led micro-infrastructure projects in Pakistan. Projects include the expansion of schools in rural and semi-rural areas, renovation and development of climate-resilient low-income housing – including houses damaged or affected by floods – and development and growth of small women-led businesses via working capital and business expansion lending. Proceeds of the PKR bond raise is anticipated to fund the issuance of at least 30,000 ~USD$290 micro-loans directly to marginalised women from 2023 to 2026. The loans will sustain existing jobs and create new jobs for women over the loan period. The Pakistan Stock Exchange predicts that achieving women’s economic empowerment in Pakistan could grow Pakistan’s economy by 60%.

description.narrative: IDI Sao Mai is a leading sustainable fish export company in Vietnam that is developing new fish processing capacity and establishing a seeding and hatching facility in Vietnam. ‍ The expanded processing facility and new seeding and hatchery will create 1,600 new local full-time jobs during the operation and management of the facility. Over 50% of the current workforce are women, and women hold 25% of the company's leadership positions. ‍ The growth in fish processing capacity will increase income generation for forty-five local farming households that are contracted to cultivate the fish. This will support diversified income generation for local farmers and improve climate resilience as they shift away from agricultural production more susceptible to climate change.

description.narrative: PIDG, through InfraCo Asia has developed grid connected rooftop solar solutions for commercial and industrial electricity customers in Nepal. Nepal’s electricity generation is heavily reliant on run-of-river hydropower, which generate more power during the rainy seasons and less during the dry summer months. This project is designed to improve the quality and diversification of electricity supply when load-shedding occurs during the summer or as weather patterns shift, affecting the supply of hydroelectricity. Over 1500 people have benefitted from increased electricity service reliability and a decrease in power shortages. ‍ Australia contributed USD 0.46m towards of a USD 2.7m multilaterally funded blended finance project.

description.narrative:
Supporting local agricultural producers through development of Cambodia’s cold chain ecosystem.
Australia has supported the development of Khmer Cold Chain warehouse, a 6000m3 facility, publicly accessible, port-linked cold storage facility in Cambodia. The cold storage facility is the first of its kind and allows smallholder farmers and small-medium agricultural enterprises to capitalise on export sales of perishable fruit and vegetables, often hindered by Cambodia’s under-developed cold chain ecosystem. The facility has a dedicated area for export services such as packaging, labelling, sanitary and phytosanitary services, and customs clearances. It provides cross-docking services to support the import and export of goods that require temperature control such as fishery products and medical goods. The cold storage facility supports local agricultural producers to meets international market safety standards and improve the shelf life of products for export, improving competitiveness of local products in the export market, in turn passing down economic efficiencies and benefits to local agricultural producers. Phase 1 of the facility became operational in 2023 and will provide access to cold chain logistics services to over 15,000 smallholder farmers in Cambodia.

description.narrative: The PIDG group operates in South and Southeast Asia to develop sustainable and climate resilient infrastructure projects. Projects include large scale renewable energy projects such as run-of-river hydro projects and solar energy. ‍ The PIDG focuses their investments on the following low emissions development pathways: ‍ •Energy and electrification – supporting the energy transition, increasing access to clean energy, and improving energy system resilience. ‍ •Transport, logistics, and connectivity – e-mobility, climate resilient telecommunications, and urban and rural logistics. ‍ •Sustainable and resilient cities and the circular economy – water and waste management, circular manufacturing, and energy-efficient, climate-adapted affordable housing. ‍ •Water and natural resource management – large-scale water utilities, manufacturing for the low-carbon transition, and financing of natural carbon sinks. ‍ In 2023, emissions avoided as a result of Australia’s funding to the PIDG totaled 2567 tCO2e.
